cases.title: CoSnitch Combined Copilot Autorun Exfiltration with a Separate Memory-Poisoning Path
cases.assessmentStatus: Retrospective public-evidence case study; not an AITBM assessment of record
cases.incidentSummary: CoSnitch covered two independent Copilot attacks. In the autorun branch the victim opened a legitimate copilot.microsoft.com URL containing an attacker prompt in ?q= together with an undocumented autorun=1 switch; the existing authenticated browser session supplied the victim context and the prompt ran without a new confirmation, instructing Copilot to retrieve information from connected Gmail, Drive, Calendar, and chat history, encode selected values into a URL, and use Copilot's own fetch capability to send the request. In the memory branch a user asked Copilot to summarize an attacker-controlled webpage; hidden page text told the system to call memory.add, and the poisoned record became future prompt context. Varonis reports that password changes, session revocation, and device re-registration did not remove the memory — it remained until explicitly deleted. Microsoft patched CVE-2026-24301 on 2026-08-18; NVD lists CVSS 8.8, required user interaction, and no known exploitation. The durable lesson the brief draws is to govern both automatic prompt execution and memory writes as security decisions.
cases.keyFinding: This is the corpus's clearest Cn-7 case that has nothing to do with compute budgets. A webpage-derived record entered durable memory with no promotion gate and no lifetime bound, and Varonis established that password change, session revocation, and device re-registration all left it in place — so the platform had no deterministic teardown for its own agent state. Unbounded state lifetime is an execution-containment failure in exactly the same sense as an unbounded loop.

aidefend.name: High-Impact Independent Validation & Approval Gate
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. A fresh decision bound to the exact prompt, connectors, data classes, destination, and intended action before connected-data access or external fetch is the Cn-6 gate that directly breaks the autorun branch; a link click and an existing login cannot approve an embedded task.

aidefend.name: Value-Level Capability Metadata & Data Flow Sink Enforcement
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Tagging Gmail, Drive, Calendar, and conversation-history values sensitive and preserving that status through encoding is the Cn-3 control that prevents the exfiltration result even when the prompt and fetch tool both execute.

aidefend.name: Transactional Promotion Gates (Quarantine -> Trusted)
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Quarantining webpage-derived memory candidates and promoting them only through an atomic, reviewed transition bound to the exact content digest is the Cn-7 state-admission control whose absence lets untrusted text become durable agent state.

aidefend.name: Inference-Time Prompt & Input Validation
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Rejecting a parameter combination that both supplies and automatically executes a prompt — or keeping q inert until the user reviews and submits it inside the authenticated session — is the Ro-1 control for the autorun ingress.

aidefend.name: Intent-Based Dynamic Capability Scoping
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Generating a short-lived connector and tool scope from a trusted user-visible task is the Pr-3 and Cn-1 control whose absence lets a URL-provided prompt reach unrelated mail, files, calendar entries, and chat history.

aidefend.name: Recalled Memory Pre-Rehydration Scanning
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Rescanning each memory record before rehydration, emitting a finding bound to the exact stored version, supplies C_monitor and behavioural-attestation evidence; the brief states it is detection and policy evidence rather than a substitute for write admission.

aidefend.name: Compromised Durable Application Session & Agent State Teardown
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Purging the exact signed conversational-memory records and independently verifying zero remaining state in scope is the Cn-7 teardown operation whose absence the brief demonstrates: password and session changes leave durable memory intact.

aidefend.name: Secure HTML Rendering & Content Demotion
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Sanitizing the summarized page into bounded plain text while retaining untrusted provenance is the Ro-1 ingress control for the memory branch; the brief marks it Medium because it constrains ingress without authorizing or blocking the memory write itself.

aidefend.name: Trust-Tiered Memory/KB Provenance & Write Eligibility Contract
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Recording caller, source, evidence, validator result, namespace, and eligibility decision for every proposed memory write supplies the facts the promotion gate consumes; the brief marks it Medium because the contract does not itself make hidden webpage text trustworthy.

cases.title: Atlassian Rovo Had Two Independent Prompt-to-Exfiltration Paths
cases.assessmentStatus: Retrospective public-evidence case study; not an AITBM assessment of record
cases.incidentSummary: Two disclosures reached the same lesson through different Rovo entry points. In RovoBlast, an authenticated user opened an Atlassian URL containing an attacker-controlled rovoChatPrompt value; Rovo treated the parameter as prompt input and started the task without a separate warning or confirmation. The URL prompt then expanded into connected-data access: the ResearchAgent could search sources available through the victim's session and permissions, and the injected instructions selected content, encoded it into an attacker-controlled URL or image request, and caused Rovo to fetch that destination. Atlassian completed a server-side remediation of that parameter route on 2026-07-08 through coordinated Bugcrowd disclosure. Separately, PromptArmor used hidden instructions in an uploaded document to make Rovo search Jira and Confluence, append results to an attacker URL, and open it — while the user had asked only to organise tickets. Disabling web search did not remove that sink: Rovo's URL-opening capability still fetched the model-constructed destination, so the vulnerable control plane was broader than the web-search setting. The brief keeps the paths separate: they are alternative entry and execution routes that converge only on the defensive lesson.
cases.keyFinding: Disabling web search did not remove the sink, and that is the scoring lesson: Cn-1 is not measured by which features are switched off but by the complete inventory of outbound-capable tools an untrusted instruction can reach. A control that governs one named capability while a generic URL-retrieval path remains unrestricted is an inventory gap, which is why this scores 0.00 rather than the 0.25 that an enforced-but-leaky boundary would earn.

aidefend.name: Value-Level Capability Metadata & Data Flow Sink Enforcement
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Marking Jira, Confluence, and other connected-source values sensitive, preserving that label through model transformations, and blocking them from attacker-selected URLs, images, or fetch requests is the shared Cn-3 control that breaks exfiltration in both branches even when retrieval is allowed.

aidefend.name: Intent-Based Dynamic Capability Scoping
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Deriving a short-lived set of data sources and tools from the user's visible task is the Pr-3 and Cn-1 control whose absence lets a ticket-organising request reach every connected source.

aidefend.name: Inference-Time Prompt & Input Validation
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Rejecting an externally supplied prompt-execution parameter at the request boundary, or making it inert display text, is the Ro-1 control for the rovoChatPrompt route; the brief notes uploaded documents need separate instruction/data and tool-policy controls.

aidefend.name: System Prompt Structure & Instruction/Data Separation
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Placing uploaded-document text in an explicitly untrusted namespace that cannot supply tool or search instructions is the Ro-1 control for the second branch.

aidefend.name: High-Impact Independent Validation & Approval Gate
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. A fresh decision bound to the exact prompt, data sources, destination, and intended output before contacting an external destination is the Cn-6 gate whose absence makes ARCR = 0 for the disclosure.

aidefend.name: Deployed AI Software Vulnerability Remediation Lifecycle
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Verifying Atlassian's 2026-07-08 server-side fix against the exact rovoChatPrompt auto-execution route, and tracking the uploaded-document disclosure as a separate finding with its own closure evidence, is the Rf remediation route.

cases.title: Rogue Agent: One Dialogflow CX Permission Crossed a Shared Project Runtime
cases.assessmentStatus: Retrospective public-evidence case study; not an AITBM assessment of record
cases.incidentSummary: Varonis showed that update rights on one Dialogflow CX agent could be converted into persistent control of a Google-managed Cloud Run execution environment shared by other agents in the same project. The starting privilege was narrow but legitimate: dialogflow.playbooks.update on one agent, enough to edit that agent's Playbook. A malicious Playbook Code Block downloaded a modified code_execution_env.py and overwrote the file in the shared managed runtime. The modified file did not remain confined to the agent whose Playbook was changed — later Code Block executions by other agents loaded the same compromised environment. After the overwrite the Playbook could be restored while the modified runtime file remained active, and Varonis reports that Cloud Logging recorded neither the file replacement nor the injected logic. The shared hook exposed several impact paths: reading conversation history and session state, sending captured data through unrestricted egress, modifying replies through respond() to insert phishing prompts, and querying the instance metadata service. The IMDS result was bounded — a token for a Google-managed, low-privilege service account — and the source does not claim it produced further escalation. Google fully remediated the affected components in June 2026.
cases.keyFinding: The blast radius came from the managed runtime boundary, not from the compromised Playbook. Tr-3 scores 0.00 rather than 0.25 because the decisive event produced no record at all and the Playbook could then be restored — so the surviving audit surface does not merely omit fields, it actively describes a state that is no longer executing. That is the difference between an incomplete log and a misleading one.

aidefend.name: Runtime Integrity Enforcement (Signed Configurations)
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Reconciling the running Code Block environment against a signed desired-state manifest before each invocation is the control that targets the persistence mechanism and the Tr-3 logging blind spot at once: a change to code_execution_env.py must stop execution even after the visible Playbook is restored.

aidefend.name: MicroVM & Low-Level Sandboxing
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. A disposable per-agent or per-invocation sandbox with no writable shared runtime layer and no access to host-management interfaces or IMDS is the Cn-1 and Cn-4 boundary whose absence lets one agent's Code Block become a project-wide execution hook.

aidefend.name: Deployed AI Software Vulnerability Remediation Lifecycle
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Confirming the managed service is on Google's June 2026 remediated control plane and retesting shared-file overwrite, cross-agent persistence, egress, and IMDS access is the Rf remediation route; the provider fix addresses the path, while customer review determines whether it was attempted before closure.

aidefend.name: Policy-Based Access Control
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Treating executable Code Block creation as a separate permission from ordinary Playbook editing, verified fail-closed against principal, project, agent, operation type, and code authority, is the Cn-2 control whose absence lets playbooks.update carry code authority.

aidefend.name: Sandbox Network Egress Restrictions
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Default-deny outbound policy enforced outside the managed runtime, with no route to IMDS, is the Cn-4 and Cn-1 boundary that limits conversation exfiltration and command-and-control even after a Code Block gains execution.

aidefend.name: Text, Markup & Structured Output Sanitization and Release Gate
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Holding chatbot responses until a release check compares them with the approved Playbook, rejecting injected reauthentication links and hidden markup, is the Cn-3 control whose absence lets respond() deliver attacker-modified replies; the brief scopes it to the phishing branch rather than to the underlying runtime compromise.

cases.title: Computer-Use TOCTOU: The Agent Clicked a Screen It Had Not Rechecked
cases.assessmentStatus: Retrospective public-evidence case study; not an AITBM assessment of record
cases.incidentSummary: A computer-use agent selected a benign Continue button from a screenshot, paused to reason, and later clicked the same coordinates after the page had replaced that control with Outlook's Send button. The page first displayed the Continue button and embedded an indirect prompt asking the agent to calculate 1+1 through bash; that harmless calculation was a timing primitive, stretching the reasoning interval by about four to five seconds. During the gap the agent retained the coordinates selected from its earlier screenshot while the page opened a prefilled Outlook compose view and aligned the Send button with the former Continue button. The agent did not re-observe the target immediately before dispatching the click, so the stale coordinate sent an email whose body and destination the attacker had already chosen. Jun Kokatsu originally reported the browser computer-use race against OpenAI Operator; Rehberger reproduced the failure class with Claude Computer Use and credited that discovery. Rehberger reports that Anthropic's Cowork added a pre-action check requiring the relevant pixels to remain unchanged, and states this is evidence for the control pattern rather than proof that every implementation enforces it.
cases.keyFinding: Computer-use agents introduce a physical gap between perception and action, and AITBM prices it as a Containment failure rather than a perception failure. The screenshot was accurate when taken and the model reasoned correctly about it; what was missing is any rule that an observation expires. Cn-6 is the sub-metric that would have caught it regardless of timing, because an email is a delegated-irreversible action and no observation, fresh or stale, authorises one.

aidefend.name: Cross-Origin Read/Write Segmentation with Step-Up Confirmation
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Re-observing the exact actionable element, origin, method, URL, and request immediately before a cross-origin browser write, and revoking the decision if the element or surrounding pixels changed, is the most specific control for the demonstrated replacement of Continue with Outlook Send.

aidefend.name: Continuous Authorization Verification (Anti-TOCTOU)
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Binding the planned click to a canonical target and live preconditions and re-checking them at dispatch is the Cn-2 control whose absence lets a decision made from one screenshot survive navigation, focus, origin, element, and visible-state changes.

aidefend.name: High-Impact Independent Validation & Approval Gate
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. A fresh approval bound to the exact account, recipient, subject, body, and Send control is the Cn-6 gate whose absence makes ARCR = 0 for the sent message.

aidefend.name: Desktop Computer-Use Workspace Isolation & Action Confirmation
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Executing only against a stable accessibility element after consuming an exact approval receipt, then reading back trusted UI or API evidence of the effect, removes coordinate-only authority and supplies the post-action result the Tr-3 record lacks.

aidefend.name: Secure HTML Rendering & Content Demotion
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Sanitizing page content into bounded plain text and preserving untrusted origin is the Ro-1 control; the brief marks it Medium because it weakens the attacker's timing setup but ordinary page changes can still create the same race.

cases.title: DuneSlide: Two LLM-Controlled Paths Escaped Cursor's Terminal Sandbox
cases.assessmentStatus: Retrospective public-evidence case study; not an AITBM assessment of record
cases.incidentSummary: DuneSlide exposed two independent Cursor 2.x flaws that converge on one asset. An indirect prompt injection delivered through malicious MCP output or poisoned web-search content could make the agent authorize an out-of-project working directory: the model selected working_directory for run_terminal_cmd and Cursor added that directory to the sandbox write allowlist without proving it remained inside the project root (CVE-2026-50548). Separately, the Write tool tried to canonicalize a destination before enforcing project scope; for a write-only symbolic link whose target did not yet exist, canonicalization failed and Cursor continued instead of denying the write (CVE-2026-50549). Either route could overwrite Cursor's cursorsandbox helper inside the application bundle, after which a later command ran without the intended terminal sandbox. The brief keeps the two phases separate: each flaw supplied a route to corrupt the enforcement component, and execution occurred when a subsequent command used that component. Cursor 3.0, released 2026-04-02, contained both fixes before Cato published on 2026-07-01.
cases.keyFinding: Cn-6 scores 0.00 for a reason the per-action view would miss: the write that overwrote cursorsandbox and the command that later ran unsandboxed are different hops, and neither is individually catastrophic. The worst-case composition rule exists precisely for this shape — an irreversible step hiding inside a chain whose visible steps look ordinary — and nothing in the assessed configuration enforced it.

aidefend.name: Tool Parameter Constraint & Schema Validation
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Making working_directory a required, typed path capability resolved by trusted code under the opened project root — canonicalizing every parent, rejecting missing or symlinked components, and passing an already-authorized directory descriptor — is the Cn-1 control that closes both the model-controlled directory escape and the check-then-reopen weakness.

aidefend.name: MicroVM & Low-Level Sandboxing
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. An operating-system sandbox below Cursor's application helper, denying writes to the application bundle even if the model, tool schema, or wrapper is compromised, is the independent Cn-1 containment layer that would bound the final execution path.

aidefend.name: Runtime Integrity Enforcement (Signed Configurations)
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Verifying the sandbox helper against a signed manifest immediately before use, and refusing execution when the running file differs from the approved release, targets the shared convergence point where both branches overwrite cursorsandbox.

aidefend.name: Deployed AI Software Vulnerability Remediation Lifecycle
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Rebuilding managed images with Cursor 3.0 or later and verifying the two disclosed paths in an isolated regression test is the Rf remediation route; the brief notes a version label alone is not closure evidence.

aidefend.name: Least-Privilege Tool Architecture
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Replacing ambient file writes with single-purpose project operations bound to object IDs or root-relative paths is the Cn-2 control whose absence let a coding agent hold a primitive able to rewrite its own enforcement helper.

cases.title: Copilot for Word Turned a Hidden Prompt into a Document-Borne AI Worm
cases.assessmentStatus: Retrospective public-evidence case study; not an AITBM assessment of record
cases.incidentSummary: A white-on-white prompt inside a Word document survived formatting removal, silently changed financial figures, and copied itself into Copilot's newly generated document. The researcher placed JSON-formatted instructions in small white text on a white background; when the document entered a Copilot for Word drafting or editing operation, formatting was stripped before model processing, so the hidden text became model-readable context competing with the user's visible request. Copilot followed the injected instruction and divided financial figures by two, making the security impact document-integrity loss rather than an unwanted reply. The same hidden prompt was written into the output document, so the instruction could run again if that output was later attached, uploaded, or selected as context. The brief is explicit that this is not autonomous network propagation: every hop depends on a user or retrieval process bringing the carrier document back into a Copilot operation. The researcher reported the issue to MSRC on 6 March; Microsoft applied mitigations and model updates in April and July, and the behaviour was still reproduced on 15 July against GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.6 deployments.
cases.keyFinding: Cp is recorded as the specification default rather than as corroborated, and that distinction is the point of the case. The failure is real and reproducible, but it terminates inside the document: nothing reached a connector, a tool, or the network, and propagation needs a person to carry the file forward. Scoring it at the ceiling on graph-derived merits would have overstated a contained integrity failure as an ungated external cascade.

aidefend.name: Text, Markup & Structured Output Sanitization and Release Gate
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. A document-specific release gate that holds the complete generated Word file, compares visible review content with the underlying text, rejects invisible or copied instructions, and blocks unsupported field changes is the Cn-3 control whose absence sets that sub-metric to 0.00; it interrupts both the tampering and the carrier-creation step.

aidefend.name: System Prompt Structure & Instruction/Data Separation
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Serializing source-document text into an explicitly non-authoritative namespace that stays structurally distinct from the user's request after formatting removal is the Cn-1 control the assessed operation lacks.

aidefend.name: High-Impact Independent Validation & Approval Gate
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Independently comparing the exact proposed changes with the visible user request, and requiring a fresh change-specific approval for unexplained value changes, is the Cn-6 gate whose absence makes ARCR = 0 for the financial edit.

aidefend.name: Inference-Time Prompt & Input Validation
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Inspecting extracted document text before prompt assembly and quarantining content that imitates instructions is the Ro-1 admission control; the brief notes it is imperfect and must be paired with the structural and output controls.

aidefend.name: Per-Prompt Content, Intent & Obfuscation Analysis
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. A pinned, calibrated detector for authority claims, instruction switching, invisible-text patterns, and copy-forward intent supplies C_monitor evidence bound to the exact content version; the brief states detection alone does not stop the edit.

cases.title: Typosquatted Agent Skills Built Reputation Before a Credential-Stealing Rug Pull
cases.assessmentStatus: Retrospective public-evidence case study; not an AITBM assessment of record
cases.incidentSummary: Zenity disrupted an active campaign that impersonated Paperclip and Browser Use through look-alike organisations, skills, repositories, and packages. The Paperclip skill family appeared on skills.sh on 5 July while its skill documents were still benign, accumulated displayed installs, and was weaponised on 11 July with instructions that steered agents to attacker-controlled code and a remote loader; malicious code had entered the surrounding repository on 6 July. A Browser Use lure instead instructed agents to install a trojanized PyPI package, browser-use-headless==0.1.4, whose helper executed credential collection on import. Recovered payloads searched more than 100 configured paths across developer, cloud, Git, package-manager, Kubernetes, Docker, infrastructure-as-code, database, and .env locations, then posted readable file contents plus host and workspace metadata to api[.]getpaperclipp[.]com/feedback inside a base64-encoded bundle. Base64 was encoding, not encryption. The reported 1.7 million figure is an aggregate displayed-install counter, not unique users or confirmed infections.
cases.keyFinding: Popularity is not provenance. Ro-4 scores 0.00 not because the skill was malicious when reviewed — it was not — but because the admission decision was never bound to the bytes it approved, so an install counter earned on 5 July still authorised different content on 11 July. That is the same failure the Behavioural Attestation Window exists to price: approval that does not expire when behaviour changes.

aidefend.name: Skill Metadata & Manifest Honesty Validation
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Detecting typosquatting and brand impersonation across skill name, author, description, source organisation, package namespace, and linked installation instructions is the Cn-5 control whose absence let look-alike identities be accepted as publishers.

aidefend.name: Manifest-vs-Observed Behavioral Consistency Testing
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Comparing attested detonation observations — downloads, process execution, file reads, network destinations — against the Skill's permission manifest is the evidence that would have marked undeclared credential collection noncompliant at admission.

aidefend.name: Admission Decision Orchestration & Triggered Revalidation
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Binding the admission decision to the exact Skill digest and invalidating it whenever instructions, repositories, releases, packages, scanners, policy, or freshness change is the Ro-4 control whose absence is the rug pull itself.

aidefend.name: Sandboxed Dependency Installation
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Installing only lockfile-pinned dependencies from a signed promoted cache inside an ephemeral no-network build container is the Ro-4 control for the Browser Use branch; it fails closed if resolution selects browser-use-headless==0.1.4.

aidefend.name: Ephemeral Single-Use Sandboxes for Tools
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Running each admitted Skill invocation once in a fresh sandbox with no developer home-directory credentials or persistent agent state is the Cn-1 containment boundary that would bound the loader after an admission miss.

aidefend.name: Skill-Level Permission Manifest Validation & Runtime Enforcement
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Requiring each Skill to declare file, network, shell, tool, and protected-resource access and enforcing that manifest at runtime is the Cn-1 control whose absence let the payload reach more than 100 credential paths and the feedback endpoint.

aidefend.name: Instruction-Layer Semantic Security Analysis
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Calibrated semantic intent classification over skill prose and progressively referenced setup documents is the Ro-1 control that targets natural-language instructions to fetch, decode, execute, and delete attacker code.

aidefend.name: Safe Ephemeral Detonation & Attested Raw Observation Reporting
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Detonating the complete installation paths in credential-free, deny-by-default microVMs produces the attested raw observations that AID-H-030.003 consumes; the brief is explicit that it supplies evidence and does not itself decide admission.

aidefend.name: Sandbox Network Egress Restrictions
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Default-deny outbound policy enforced outside the sandboxed process is the Cn-1 egress boundary that would have blocked the disclosed loader and feedback endpoints even after admission missed the payload.

cases.title: Miasma Targets Repository-Local Trust in Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Cursor, and VS Code
cases.assessmentStatus: Retrospective public-evidence case study; not an AITBM assessment of record
cases.incidentSummary: On 2026-06-05 a previously compromised contributor account pushed commit 5f456b8 to Azure/durabletask. The commit was backdated, carried [skip ci], added five files, and changed no application source. Four of the files were repository-local trigger configurations; the fifth was a 4.6 MB obfuscated .github/setup.js credential harvester. Opening the project could launch that payload through Claude Code or Gemini CLI SessionStart hooks or a Cursor always-applied rule — and, on a separate non-AI path outside this assessment, a VS Code folder-open task. Once launched the harvester ran with the developer process's local access. GitHub later disabled 73 repositories across four Microsoft organisations in two automated waves; StepSecurity confirms the malicious commit in Azure/durabletask but does not establish that the payload propagated into every disabled repository.
cases.keyFinding: Miasma moves supply-chain execution from package installation to project open, and AITBM records that as an identity failure as much as a containment one: Cn-5 scores 0.00 because nothing bound the agent's operating directive to a verified source, so a repository rather than the operator defined what the agent would do at startup. The non-AI VS Code route is deliberately excluded from the assessed system — the brief's own defence descriptions disclaim coverage of it, and folding it in would have mixed a conventional IDE trust boundary into an AI-agent score.

aidefend.name: Client-Side Configuration Enforcement
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Scanning repository-local Claude Code, Gemini CLI, and Cursor configuration before commit or checkout acceptance — and enforcing policy against SessionStart command hooks, always-applied execution instructions, backdated skip-CI commits, and unexpected executable references — is the Ro-4 and Ro-1 admission control the disclosed path lacks. The brief states this control does not cover the separate non-AI VS Code folder-open route, which this workpaper also excludes.

aidefend.name: Runtime Integrity Enforcement (Signed Configurations)
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Rejecting unsigned local configuration overrides at agent startup, and requiring approved signed configuration before a hook or rule can run, is the Cn-5 control whose absence lets a repository define the agent's directive.

aidefend.name: Runtime Configuration & Policy Drift Detection and Monitoring
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Alerting on configuration-only commits that suppress CI or introduce new automatic execution paths is the C_monitor evidence the assessed environment does not produce; it is detection, not enforcement.

aidefend.name: MicroVM & Low-Level Sandboxing
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. cases.title: Ray DNS Rebinding: A Malicious Page Reaches the Local Jobs API
cases.assessmentStatus: Retrospective public-evidence case study; not an AITBM assessment of record
cases.incidentSummary: CVE-2025-62593 affects Ray before 2.52.0. A developer running the Ray Dashboard on its default port can be compromised after visiting a malicious page or advertisement in Firefox or Safari. Ray blocked POST and PUT only when the User-Agent header began with 'Mozilla'; both browsers allow JavaScript to set another value, so the request no longer looked like browser traffic to the middleware. DNS rebinding then repointed the attacker's origin at port 8265 on localhost or a private Ray host, and page JavaScript submitted an unauthenticated job containing attacker-selected commands, which Ray executed. The advisory's proof of concept opens Calculator; broader payloads are possible but are not evidence of a specific observed campaign. CISA added the CVE to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-08-17 without attributing the exploitation.
cases.keyFinding: Three boundaries each failed independently — an origin heuristic mistaken for identity, network reachability from a browser process to a management port, and an unauthenticated execution API — and the case scores 0.00 on all three Containment sub-metrics because a spoofable self-asserted header is not a control at any anchor. Ray 2.52.0 closes the disclosed path, but Cn-5 stays at 0.00 for any deployment that still authorises job submission by inspecting what the caller claims to be.

aidefend.name: Service & API Authentication
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Authenticated, short-lived caller credentials on every Ray Jobs and job-agent API request is the Cn-5 control whose absence sets that sub-metric to 0.00; the advisory states directly that a browser-origin heuristic is not an identity control.

aidefend.name: Deployed AI Software Vulnerability Remediation Lifecycle
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Reconciling all Ray installations and redeploying 2.52.0 or later with verification of the running dashboard process is the Rf remediation route; it is not IVP evidence for this case.

aidefend.name: Internal AI Network Segmentation
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Binding development dashboards to an explicitly controlled interface and using host firewalls or microsegmentation so browser processes and untrusted network zones cannot reach Ray management APIs is the Cn-1 boundary the assessed configuration places outside the product because it has none inside it.

cases.title: MLflow Webhook Redirects Turn a Public URL into Full-Read SSRF
cases.assessmentStatus: Retrospective public-evidence case study; not an AITBM assessment of record
cases.incidentSummary: CVE-2026-64849 affects MLflow through 3.13.0. On a default Tracking Server, webhook management and the synchronous test endpoint are unauthenticated. An attacker registers a public HTTPS webhook, triggers its test, and returns a 302 redirect to a loopback, private-network, or cloud-metadata URL. MLflow validates only the original hostname; it follows the redirect without validating or pinning the destination and reflects the internal response body back to the caller. The advisory demonstrates a local secret service and identifies cloud instance metadata and internal admin services as reachable targets. CISA added the CVE to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-08-19 without publishing exploitation details. The advisory lists a code fix — PR #24258, which validates each connected peer including redirect targets — but GitHub lists no patched version, so no minimum safe release exists.
cases.keyFinding: Cn-1 scores 0.25 rather than 0.00 even though the SSRF succeeded completely, because AITBM scores the boundary that exists rather than the outcome that occurred: MLflow did have a destination policy and it did reject direct private-range URLs. What it lacked was binding that decision to the connection actually made — the distinction between a check and an enforcement point, which is exactly the gap between the 0.25 and 0.50 anchors.

aidefend.name: URL Normalization & Allowlist Filtering
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. A fail-closed safe fetcher that validates every redirect target, connects only to the freshly validated public IP, and binds the decision to the final URL and returned bytes is the Cn-1 control whose absence produces the validation-to-use gap; it closes both the redirect and DNS-rebinding TOCTOU paths.

aidefend.name: Service & API Authentication
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Authenticated, short-lived credentials for webhook creation and test operations, enforced on the server-side API path rather than through network reachability, is the Cn-5 control the default configuration does not load.

aidefend.name: Internal AI Network Segmentation
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Least-privilege internal network policy so the MLflow workload cannot reach instance metadata, loopback-admin bridges, or unrelated private services is the compensating boundary that would bound Cp even when application URL validation fails.

aidefend.name: Deployed AI Software Vulnerability Remediation Lifecycle
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Tracking every instance through 3.13.0 as vulnerable and deploying a vendor release containing PR #24258 only after its exact artefact is available and verified is the Rf remediation route; it is not IVP evidence for this case.

cases.title: Flowise CSV Agent: Prompt Injection Bypasses a Regex Blocklist and Reaches Host-Capable Pyodide
cases.assessmentStatus: Retrospective public-evidence case study; not an AITBM assessment of record
cases.incidentSummary: CVE-2026-70477 affects Flowise and flowise-components through 3.1.2 and is fixed in 3.1.3. An unauthenticated attacker sends instructions to a chatflow containing a CSV Agent. The LLM returns obfuscated Python; the static regex blocklist in validatePythonCodeForDataFrame() accepts it; Flowise passes the code to Pyodide. Because that runtime was not isolated from host operating-system interfaces, the payload executes with the privileges of the user running the Flowise server. The advisory demonstrates eight bypass variants — string concatenation, chr() encoding, builtin aliasing, frame inspection, MRO traversal, df.query(), and decorator-based indirect execution — establishing that the denylist is a class-level failure rather than a single missed pattern. The advisory states the route is conditional: it requires a reachable chatflow using the affected node and an LLM response that produces a working bypass.
cases.keyFinding: A denylist is not an admission gate. The control that was present ran on every snippet and still scored only 0.25, because Cn-3 measures survival under systematic evasion and eight independent working bypasses are exactly that evidence; meanwhile the two boundaries that would have contained the failure — an input gate and an execution sandbox — were absent entirely and scored 0.00.

aidefend.name: Pre-Execution Static Analysis & Dangerous Construct Blocking
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Replacing the regex denylist with a fail-closed, signed-policy AST admission gate over the exact Python bytes is the control whose absence sets Cn-3 at 0.25 rather than higher; a clean AST result still does not prove arbitrary code safe.

aidefend.name: Safe Interpreter Enforcement
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Routing permitted evaluations only to an explicitly allowlisted restricted interpreter, chosen by an execution gateway rather than by the model, is the Cn-3 enforcement layer the assessed configuration lacks.

aidefend.name: Ephemeral Single-Use Sandboxes for Tools
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. A fresh single-use microVM, gVisor, or Kata boundary per evaluation, with the Flowise host process, filesystem, credentials, and management plane outside it, is the Cn-1 control whose absence the advisory states directly.

aidefend.name: Deployed AI Software Vulnerability Remediation Lifecycle
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Reconciling the deployed Flowise population against the advisory and redeploying 3.1.3 or later with digest-level completion evidence is the Rf remediation route; it is not IVP evidence for this case.

aidefend.name: Inference-Time Prompt & Input Validation
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. A calibrated prompt-injection gate before the primary LLM is the missing Ro-1 control. The brief marks its contribution 'Partial' because it is a bounded first layer that cannot replace executable-artifact admission or runtime isolation.

cases.title: Deadbugz: GitHub PRs Delivered a Delayed, Shape-Shifting Malicious MCP Server
cases.assessmentStatus: Retrospective public-evidence case study; not an AITBM assessment of record
cases.incidentSummary: Pillar Security documented Deadbugz, an active campaign that opened 23 GitHub pull requests in about 74 minutes to place a malicious MCP server in popular repositories and MCP directories. The server behaved normally at first, then changed later tool descriptions and prompt content into instructions for credential discovery, covert file access, command execution, and exfiltration. None of the reviewed pull requests was merged, and the public evidence does not show victim execution or confirmed data theft.
cases.keyFinding: MCP onboarding cannot be a one-time trust decision: clients must bind descriptor and prompt semantics, detect drift, and re-authorize every consequential action against current user intent.

aidefend.name: Client-Side Configuration Enforcement
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Validate every proposed MCP configuration against a strict schema and policy before commit or build acceptance. Reject unapproved remote endpoints, hidden local script paths, and configurations that grant broad client capabilities; require protected branches and code-owner review for production configuration. This blocks the delivery path before a Deadbugz pull request can make the server available to users. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

aidefend.name: MCP Tool Descriptor Hash Binding & Drift Detection
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Canonicalize every approved MCP tool descriptor, pin its digest during onboarding, and compare each later tools/list response with that manifest before exposing it to the agent. Deadbugz changed descriptor text after benign calls, so a mismatch can fail closed before the injected instructions reach the privileged model. This control applies to tool descriptors, not to prompts/get content. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

aidefend.name: Approved Tool Contract Semantics & Change Admission
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Encode policy checks for each MCP tool's approved operation, side effects, privilege scope, and destructive behavior. Bind the exact descriptor and semantic profile to a signed approval, and require a new security review whenever either changes. This catches malicious initial contracts as well as Deadbugz's delayed change in tool meaning. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

aidefend.name: Intent-Based Dynamic Capability Scoping
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. At the start of each request or session, intersect the authenticated user's stated task with the exact versioned tool registry, action budget, and grant lifetime, then enforce that signed scope at the dispatcher. A formatting or summarization task should never receive credential-reading, shell, email, or repository-write capabilities, so the poisoned instructions have no matching authority to invoke. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

aidefend.name: Least-Privilege Tool Architecture
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Expose only allowlisted, strongly typed, single-purpose tools with bounded paths, destinations, credentials, and side effects. Remove generic shell, broad filesystem, arbitrary HTTP, and equivalent ambient-power tools from the agent. Even if poisoned MCP text reaches the model, it no longer has a general mechanism for reading credential files, running arbitrary commands, or sending data anywhere. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

aidefend.name: High-Impact Independent Validation & Approval Gate
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Before executing code, sending email, changing a repository, or reading a protected credential path, independently validate the exact immutable action, target, parameters, current identity, and signed policy. When policy requires approval, bind it to that same action and consume it once at the executor. Attacker-authored MCP text cannot serve as authorization for the requested effect. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

aidefend.name: Value-Level Capability Metadata & Data Flow Sink Enforcement
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Attach provenance and sensitivity labels to values read from credential paths, shell history, or Kubernetes configuration, then enforce sink policy at command, email, network, and repository dispatch. This blocks a sensitive value from leaving through a tool even if the model follows the injected instructions. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

aidefend.name: Confirmed Malicious Code & Persistence Eviction
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. If investigation confirms that a Deadbugz configuration, script, package, or startup artifact was installed, remove the exact object from every authoritative configuration source and loaded runtime, preserve evidence, and verify that no runtime can load it again. This contains an installed artifact but does not replace review of actions already performed. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

aidefend.name: Root & Long-Lived Credential Object Eviction
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. When evidence shows that a password, API key, SSH private key, client secret, or other long-lived credential was read or exposed, enumerate the exact affected objects and revoke, disable, or rotate them at every authoritative issuer and verifier. This is incident-scoped containment after exposure, not a reason to rotate all credentials based only on the presence of a malicious pull request. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

cases.title: Stolen Thoughts: Opaque Reasoning Blocks Could Be Replayed to Recover Secrets
cases.assessmentStatus: Retrospective public-evidence case study; not an AITBM assessment of record
cases.incidentSummary: Stolen Thoughts found that opaque reasoning blocks returned by Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google APIs could be accepted across sessions, users, or compatible models within a provider family. An attacker who first obtained another user's block could submit it to a weaker compatible model and jailbreak that model into transcribing hidden reasoning. In 6,708 public agent trajectories, the researchers reconstructed 315,320 blocks and found real sensitive artifacts in 328 sessions. They report that provider mitigations later made the demonstrated attacks non-reproducible.
cases.keyFinding: Opaque state is not safe state: reasoning artifacts need confidentiality, principal/session binding, bounded retention, and an output gate before they enter logs or client-visible trajectories.

aidefend.name: Reasoning-Trace Confidentiality & Storage Controls
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Keep full reasoning blocks in provider-side or protected server-side state, classify them as sensitive, and deny their display, client return, analytics export, and public logging. Publish only bounded summaries or non-reversible references. This removes the portable artifact that the third-party attack must first acquire. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

aidefend.name: Provider Reasoning-Block Round-Trip Integrity
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Preserve provider-authored reasoning blocks byte-for-byte in a server-held envelope, return them only through the same provider route and conversation, verify provider binding where supported, and reject client-supplied or altered blocks before continuation. This blocks the captured-block replay path for an integration that enforces the boundary, but it does not repair a provider API that accepts the same block through a direct path outside that integration. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

aidefend.name: Task-Bounded Context Segmentation & Secret Demotion
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Keep credentials and other high-sensitivity values outside conversation and model context. Give the agent short-lived, task-scoped handles that an authorized broker resolves only at the approved tool or network sink. If the underlying value never enters model context, it cannot be captured inside a reasoning block; this does not protect proprietary reasoning that legitimately remains there. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

aidefend.name: Automated Agentic Security Benchmarking
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Turn the paper's captured-block, compatible-model, and transcription-jailbreak cases into a signed, sanitized regression corpus. Block each model or API release unless it rejects the replay path and prevents sensitive plaintext from being released. This tests the demonstrated bypass as models and routing change; it does not prove universal jailbreak resistance. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

aidefend.name: Sensitive Information & Data Leakage Detection
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Inspect the complete decoder response before delivery. Detect common credential formats with deterministic patterns and use structured PII detection for names, addresses, email addresses, and other unstructured personal data, then emit findings to the release gate. Detection identifies recognizable sensitive content but does not stop delivery by itself. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

aidefend.name: Text, Markup & Structured Output Sanitization and Release Gate
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Hold the complete decoder response or a bounded release unit until sensitive-output findings have been evaluated. Apply deterministic redaction or denial, and fail closed if the gate cannot complete. This can block recognizable credentials and personal data in recovered plaintext, but it cannot prove that all proprietary reasoning has been removed. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

aidefend.name: Root & Long-Lived Credential Object Eviction
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. When evidence proves that a password, API key, client secret, private key, or other root or long-lived credential appeared in exposed reasoning plaintext, enumerate the exact incident-scoped objects and revoke, disable, reset, or rotate them at every authoritative issuer and verifier. This is post-exposure containment, not prevention of reasoning extraction. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

aidefend.name: Issued Token, Authentication Session & Lease Revocation
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. If the exposed material includes access tokens, refresh tokens, session cookies, authorization-server sessions, gateway sessions, or agent leases, revoke the complete affected population at every issuer, verifier, cache, and enforcement point. Rotating a long-lived credential does not invalidate these already-issued objects, so they require a separate response action. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

cases.title: LangSmith Tracing Header Injection Turned Observability Metadata into a Data Route
cases.assessmentStatus: Retrospective public-evidence case study; not an AITBM assessment of record
cases.incidentSummary: CVE-2026-25528 affected applications that passed untrusted HTTP tracing headers into the LangSmith SDK. A crafted baggage header could add an attacker-controlled replica URL; when a traced operation finished, the SDK sent run data to that destination. Inputs, outputs, and application metadata could therefore leave through a feature intended for observability. The flaw shows that tracing context is active routing authority, not harmless metadata.
cases.keyFinding: Observability metadata is routing authority when it can select an exporter; trace context must be schema-restricted, destination-pinned, and minimized before export.

aidefend.name: Deployed AI Software Vulnerability Remediation Lifecycle
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Inventory the Python and npm LangSmith SDK versions actually loaded by each service, rebuild on the current supported releases, stage rollout, and use runtime or image readback to prove vulnerable packages have exited. This removes the SDK behavior that accepted a caller-controlled replica destination. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

aidefend.name: Inference Telemetry & Debug Surface Restriction
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Before any trace leaves the inference service, suppress or redact prompts, outputs, retrieved context, tool arguments, secrets, and unnecessary metadata, then fail closed if the exporter cannot prove the policy is active. This reduces what an injected or misconfigured destination can receive, but it does not repair destination selection. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

aidefend.name: Secure External AI Service Connectivity
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Give tracing workloads default-deny egress and allow only approved LangSmith endpoints through verified DNS and SNI policy. An attacker-controlled replica URL, or an internal metadata destination, then fails at a network boundary independent of the SDK parser. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

aidefend.name: Inference-Time Prompt & Input Validation
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. At request ingress, parse baggage with a strict schema and a safe-field allowlist, reject unknown replica fields, and remove caller-controlled api_url , api_key , or equivalent authority before tracing context is created. This is structured-header validation, not a prompt-injection filter. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

cases.title: SGLang's ZMQ and Pickle Paths Show Why Internal AI Messages Need a Trust Boundary
cases.assessmentStatus: Retrospective public-evidence case study; not an AITBM assessment of record
cases.incidentSummary: CERT/CC reported three Python pickle deserialization RCE paths in SGLang: two required optional distributed features enabled and unauthenticated ZeroMQ ports reachable, while the third required an operator to replay a malicious request dump. Because public patch notes and current CNA disclosures disagree on fixed versions, defenders should verify runtime configuration and peer reachability instead of relying only on package version strings.
cases.keyFinding: An internal AI message bus is still an untrusted code boundary: peer identity, segmentation, and safe serialization must hold before bytes reach a deserializer.

aidefend.name: Deployed AI Software Vulnerability Remediation Lifecycle
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Inventory the running SGLang package version and image digest; if confirmed vulnerable, upgrade immediately to the supported release. If an immediate upgrade is delayed, temporarily disable affected optional features, rebuild on the fixed version, stage deployment, and verify older workloads have exited. Because public sources conflict on version 0.5.10, runtime config checks and peer connectivity tests are mandatory. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

aidefend.name: Internal AI Network Segmentation
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Restrict ZeroMQ ports to required peer IPs with host firewalls and default-deny NetworkPolicy. This blocks untrusted network traffic before it reaches pickle deserialization, even if cross-node configuration overrides the loopback default. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

aidefend.name: Service & API Authentication
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Enforce mTLS or workload identity for cross-host broker traffic to require caller authentication and scope access. This removes implicit trust from internal ports, though transport authentication cannot neutralize malicious data from a compromised peer. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

aidefend.name: Container-Based Isolation
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Run SGLang as non-root with a read-only filesystem, minimal mounts, no production secrets, and resource caps. If deserialization executes code, these boundaries limit file, identity, and lateral access, containing impact rather than fixing the parser. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

cases.title: Pydantic AI Shows How Message History Can Become Server-Side Fetch Authority
cases.assessmentStatus: Retrospective public-evidence case study; not an AITBM assessment of record
cases.incidentSummary: CVE-2026-25580 let untrusted Pydantic AI message history and URL-based attachments cause the application server to fetch attacker-selected addresses. A crafted file URL could reach internal services, link-local cloud metadata, or other destinations unavailable to the external caller. Two later IPv6-transition bypasses affected applications that explicitly allowed local downloads. The case shows that a serialized conversation is not passive history when replaying it invokes server-side I/O.
cases.keyFinding: Serialized conversation history is active authority when deserialization triggers I/O; replay paths require the same destination policy as an explicit network tool call.

aidefend.name: Deployed AI Software Vulnerability Remediation Lifecycle
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Reconcile the Pydantic AI version running in every application with all three advisories, rebuild on the current supported release, stage deployment, and read back the fleet to prove older packages and images have exited. This avoids stopping at 1.56.0 while later transition-address bypasses remain in scope. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

aidefend.name: URL Normalization & Allowlist Filtering
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Before the server fetches any message-history URL, canonicalize it, resolve and pin the destination, reject private, loopback, link-local, metadata, and IPv6-transition ranges, validate every redirect, and return bytes from that same verified connection. This is the direct control for the original SSRF and its parser-versus-network bypasses. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

aidefend.name: Secure External AI Service Connectivity
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Apply default-deny egress to the application workload and allow only approved external services through verified DNS and SNI policy, with cloud metadata explicitly blocked. This provides a network backstop if application validation is bypassed, although it cannot decide whether an allowed public URL is safe for the business context. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

aidefend.name: Inference-Time Prompt & Input Validation
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Validate the untrusted message-history schema at ingress, allow only required URL-part types, reject unknown fields, and prevent callers from setting force_download or an equivalent local-fetch override. This removes unsafe authority from the serialized request, but a syntactically valid URL still needs the dedicated safe-fetch checks in AID-H-019.001. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

cases.title: MCFA Turns Agent Memory into a Delayed Control-Flow Input
cases.assessmentStatus: Retrospective public-evidence case study; not an AITBM assessment of record
cases.incidentSummary: Memory Control Flow Attacks (MCFA) do not need direct access to an agent's memory database or system prompt. The research shows how ordinary interaction can place an action-oriented preference into long-term memory, then a later benign task retrieves it and changes tool choice or order. Across controlled LangChain and LlamaIndex experiments, tool-selection attacks were highly reliable, while ordering attacks were weaker. Memory must therefore be governed as persistent control input, not trusted conversation history.
cases.keyFinding: Long-term memory is persistent control input: every write needs provenance and promotion policy, and every recall must be re-authorized against the current task before it can influence tools.

aidefend.name: Transactional Promotion Gates (Quarantine -> Trusted)
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Route every untrusted or high-risk new memory record to quarantine, then promote the exact version through an atomic, evidence-backed state transition before it becomes retrieval-eligible. This directly interrupts MCFA's first stage by preventing an ordinary low-trust conversation write from silently becoming trusted control input. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

aidefend.name: High-Impact Independent Validation & Approval Gate
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. At the executor boundary, independently validate the canonical action, caller identity, policy evidence, and exact approval for high-impact operations. Even when malicious memory succeeds in changing the plan or tool order, the recalled text cannot authorize a transfer, deletion, credential change, or other side effect by itself. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

aidefend.name: Persistent Memory Partitioning (Trust & Tenant Isolation)
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Partition persistent memory by tenant and trust tier, and make retrieval consult centralized entitlement policy before a record enters the model context. This limits cross-user and low-trust recall, but the paper's RBMS results show that segregation plus prompt hierarchy is not a complete defense when models fail to honor the hierarchy. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

aidefend.name: Recalled Memory Pre-Rehydration Scanning
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. After loading an exact versioned memory record and before adding it to the prompt, rescan it for role or authority assertions, trigger-like markers, encoded fragments, known quarantine fingerprints, and policy risk, then emit a content-bound finding that downstream policy can quarantine or omit. This places inspection at MCFA's second stage, although semantic instructions can evade detection and a finding is not enforcement by itself. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

aidefend.name: Tool-Call Sequence Anomaly Detection
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Learn approved tool transitions and detect forbidden, low-likelihood, or missing-stage sequences, such as a transfer tool appearing before its required audit step. This is especially relevant to MCFA Order attacks and can surface successful steering, but it detects a changed trace after planning rather than preventing the memory write. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Record who proposed each memory item, the supporting evidence, validator result, namespace, trust tier, and recommended retrieval eligibility, including contradiction checks against authoritative facts. This creates the decision facts a promotion gate needs; it classifies and preserves provenance but does not enforce admission on its own. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

cases.title: Poisoned GGUF Chat Templates Backdoor Inference Without Changing Model Weights
cases.assessmentStatus: Retrospective public-evidence case study; not an AITBM assessment of record
cases.incidentSummary: Researchers from Pillar Security and Fujitsu showed that a GGUF artifact can carry a modified Jinja chat template while its model weights remain unchanged. When a trigger appears, the inference engine renders attacker instructions into system-level context before the model runs; controlled tests degraded model behavior and hijacked BrowserUse and OpenHands tool use. Defenders need to treat chat templates as executable release artifacts, verify their exact bytes and provenance, regression-test every conversion, and enforce tool and data-flow boundaries.
cases.keyFinding: Model weights are only one executable release component; chat templates must be digest-bound, provenance-checked, and security-regression-tested with the same rigor as the weights.

aidefend.name: Post-Training Optimization & Format-Conversion Safety Regression
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Treat every GGUF conversion or repackaging step as a security-relevant transformation. Bind the candidate to approved source bytes and conversion settings, then compare both artifacts on the same signed suite for trigger-conditioned behavior, instruction-hierarchy changes, leakage, and tool-policy violations. Block promotion when lineage is missing or any security category regresses. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

aidefend.name: CI/CD Release Gating, Model Artifact Signing & Secure Distribution
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Production should load only reviewed, signed, digest-pinned GGUF bytes from an internal mirror. The promotion gate should verify the artifact source, complete digest, bundled template, loader policy, regression evidence, and approval record before deployment or hot reload. A public model name or unchanged weight hash is not sufficient admission evidence. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

aidefend.name: Model SBOM & Provenance Attestation
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Bind the complete GGUF digest, model format, source, loader commit, tokenizer, and configuration evidence into a signed model SBOM and attestation. Verify the signature, predicate, signer identity, and actual artifact digest before admission and every load. This proves that the runtime received the approved bytes; it does not determine whether the bundled Jinja logic is semantically safe. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

aidefend.name: Value-Level Capability Metadata & Data Flow Sink Enforcement
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. For BrowserUse or another live action that actually passes through the governed dispatcher, require a server-side content identifier for payment fields, personal data, credentials, or repository content. Deny labelled content at attacker-controlled network, write, or file sinks, and keep agent egress default-deny. This control does not govern an OpenHands-generated script after the code leaves that dispatcher. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

cases.title: Model Namespace Reuse Turns a Trusted Name Into a Supply-Chain Redirect
cases.assessmentStatus: Retrospective public-evidence case study; not an AITBM assessment of record
cases.incidentSummary: Unit 42 showed that a deleted Hugging Face author namespace, or a transferred model whose former author namespace later becomes reclaimable, can leave stale references pointing to a name another party can register. In controlled tests, researchers reclaimed abandoned namespaces, recreated expected model paths, and made Vertex AI and Azure AI Foundry deployments load reverse-shell models. The original publisher account was not compromised. Defenders should bind deployments to immutable digests and signers, monitor namespace lifecycles, mirror approved artifacts internally, and isolate model loading.
cases.keyFinding: A familiar model name is not an identity: deployment admission must bind approved bytes, signer, source ownership, and loader policy before first load and every reload.

aidefend.name: Model SBOM & Provenance Attestation
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Bind every approved model to its exact artifact digest, signer identity, source URL, author namespace, source commit, format, and loader in a signed model SBOM. Admission and reload checks should reject any new bytes or signer behind the same familiar name and deny use when a verified upstream namespace or owner tombstone applies. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

aidefend.name: CI/CD Release Gating, Model Artifact Signing & Secure Distribution
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Production systems should never pull a model directly from a public namespace by name. Mirror reviewed bytes into an internal registry, pin their immutable digest, and require the promotion gate to re-verify owner, source, redirects, signature, model format, loader policy, and tombstone state before deployment or hot reload. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

aidefend.name: Sandbox Network Egress Restrictions
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Load and evaluate third-party model candidates in a sandbox with default-deny outbound traffic and only narrowly approved destinations. The demonstrated payload required an outbound reverse-shell callback, so an enforcement point outside the model process can stop that connection even after malicious code starts. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

aidefend.name: MicroVM & Low-Level Sandboxing
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Place first load and evaluation inside a stronger-than-container boundary with no production secrets, shared home directory, host mounts, or broad syscall access. If a substituted model executes code, the microVM or userspace-kernel sandbox keeps the foothold away from the deployment host, internal services, and credential stores. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

aidefend.name: Model Source & Namespace Drift Detection
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. During model curation, alert when an external model reference starts returning 404 or 3xx responses because those lifecycle changes can precede namespace replacement. Independently monitor production DNS and egress for unexpected contact with public model hubs, preserving the source URL and prior ownership state needed to investigate drift. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

cases.title: ZombieAgent Shows How Connector Prompt Injection Can Persist and Spread
cases.assessmentStatus: Retrospective public-evidence case study; not an AITBM assessment of record
cases.incidentSummary: Radware showed how hidden instructions in email or documents read through ChatGPT connectors could turn a task into data exfiltration. Fixed URLs encoded stolen text one character per request, Memory preserved instructions across chats, and a contact-harvesting branch spread the payload; Radware says OpenAI fixed it on December 16, 2025. Workspace administrators can disable unnecessary connectors or Memory and narrow or revoke grants, while platform implementers own raw-content isolation, Memory gates, and default-deny egress; value-level sink checks cover only explicit transfers retaining server-side content IDs.
cases.keyFinding: Persistent memory changes prompt injection from a one-chat event into delayed control flow; trusted intent must govern both memory promotion and every later rehydration.

aidefend.name: Dual-LLM Isolation Pattern
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Send raw email, documents, and connector content only to a quarantined model with no privileged tools. A validating broker may release only allowlisted domain fields and opaque record identifiers in a signed envelope; a generic free-text summary is not a security boundary. The privileged model never receives the original attacker text, and every proposal still goes through the executor's authorization checks. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

aidefend.name: Transactional Promotion Gates (Quarantine -> Trusted)
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Externally influenced content must not write directly into trusted Memory. Store proposed memories in quarantine with tenant, source, content digest, and target namespace, then require a content-bound approval and controlled-writer receipt before atomic promotion. Prompt assembly must exclude every pending or rejected state. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

aidefend.name: Value-Level Capability Metadata & Data Flow Sink Enforcement
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Put URL fetches, remote subresources, and outbound mail behind default-deny provider egress with a change-managed destination allowlist. For explicit value transfers that already carry a server-side content identifier, apply the labelled sink policy at dispatch. This blocks the attacker domain in the demonstrated chain, but the current guidance does not automatically track the implicit flow in which a secret character selects one prebuilt URL. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

aidefend.name: Intent-Based Dynamic Capability Scoping
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Register connector read, Memory write, web open, and outbound message as distinct tool names. Derive the signed set of allowed names, action budget, and expiry from the authenticated user's visible request, so an inbox-reading task cannot acquire unrelated tools from retrieved text. This guidance does not constrain mailbox resources or result cardinality inside one broadly designed connector operation. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

aidefend.name: Recalled Memory Pre-Rehydration Scanning
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. Before any saved Memory record re-enters prompt assembly, scan the exact versioned content for authority claims, delayed triggers, encoded fragments, and known quarantine fingerprints. Bind the finding to the tenant, record version, content digest, detector revision, and policy. This detector only recommends a disposition; a downstream Harden or Isolate policy must decide and enforce blocking or quarantine. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.

aidefend.name: Text, Markup & Structured Output Sanitization and Release Gate
aidefend.note: AIDEFEND dataVersion 2026.09.20. For the renderer-based branch, hold generated output until remote subresources and URLs have passed sink-specific policy. Remove or proxy unapproved images and previews, disable automatic fetches, and verify with browser-egress tests that Markdown, HTML, CSS, SVG, and reference links cannot silently trigger the fixed-URL requests. This relationship is an evidence route only and supplies no positive score credit without observed control operation.
